title: eval-harness: integrate per-prompt regression metrics into CI hooks
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Our per-prompt regression checks currently surface only pass/fail gating which hides subtle metric regressions (e.g. BLEU/ROUGE/accuracy drift) that accumulate over time. This PR adds an integration that pushes per-prompt evaluation metrics into the CI hooks so the pipeline can fail on statistically significant regressions and also post metric deltas to PR threads. Summary: - Compute per-prompt and aggregated metrics (accuracy/acceptance rate/weighted-rouge) for new eval runs - Persist a small metrics artifact and compare to stored baseline per prompt set - Fail CI when regression exceeds configurable thresholds or when metric noise is low and negative drift is detected - Post a summarized metrics table and links to the detailed artifact in the PR comments - Add a lightweight metrics uploader and a stable comparator used by both hosted CI and local dev runs Checklist: - [x] Add metrics collection in eval runner and export to JSON artifacts - [x] Implement comparator with configurable thresholds and sample-size-aware z-test - [x] Wire comparator into CI hook and post PR comment with results - [x] Add unit tests for comparator and end-to-end test in the CI matrix - [x] Add docs and config example for teams to opt in/backfill baselines Backwards compatibility: The integration is opt-in via eval-harness/ci/config/prompt_metrics.yml and will not change default gating behavior until teams enable it. Testing: Unit tests added under eval-harness/tests/test_metrics_comparator.py. End-to-end CI job added to .github/workflows/eval-ci.yaml (matrix entry). Observability: The CI comment includes links to the artifact bucket and a compact CSV for point-in-time analysis. Rollout plan: Merge to main; feature gate turned off by default; enable for a small set of internal prompt-sets for two weeks; iterate on thresholds based on observed false positives. Notes: I intentionally kept the comparator implementation small and well-documented to allow reuse by downstream Dedicated/private pipelines. See linked Linear items for follow-ups on metric normalization and historic baseline maintenance.
